title: Ito events
description: Everything the server says on `GET /v0/events`. Each Server-Sent Event carries one event: its `id:` line is the event's id and its `data:` line is the event as JSON. Apps skip event types they don't recognise, but still keep their id as the cursor.

Event.description: One event on the stream; its `type` says which.

EventId.description: Opaque and never reused, even after the server is restored from a backup. Resume by sending the id of the last event you applied as `Last-Event-ID`.

MessageId.description: Opaque. The app makes the ids of the messages you send (random UUIDs); the server makes the ids of the agent's messages.

TurnId.description: Opaque. A turn is one run of the agent, from its inputs to an answer, a stop or an error.

StepId.description: Opaque. The server makes it when a step starts.

AskId.description: Opaque. The server makes it when the agent asks.

AttachmentId.description: Opaque: the `UploadId` the app made for what it uploaded, or an id the server made for a recording it keeps, such as a spoken message's.

UploadId.description: A random UUID, in lowercase, the app makes before uploading. It is the attachment's id and its retry key.

TopicId.description: Opaque. The server makes it when Ari marks a topic.

CallId.description: A random UUID the app makes when you start a call.

Timestamp.description: Server time, RFC 3339 in UTC with milliseconds.

Position.description: Where a message or a step sits in the conversation: strictly increasing in conversation order, with gaps. Snapshots and history pages carry messages and steps in separate lists; merge them by position.

Outcome.description: How a message or a turn ended: `completed`; `stopped` by you; `interrupted` because the server restarted; or `failed`, with an error. Treat an outcome you don't recognise as ended.

Error.description: Why something failed. A failed turn uses `model_timeout`, `model_unavailable`, `usage_limit`, `engine_signed_out`, `context_full`, `engine_failed`, `server_disk_full`, `refused` or `internal`. A refused command uses `invalid_request`, `token_rejected`, `pairing_code_rejected`, `not_found`, `id_conflict`, `too_large`, `attachment_missing`, `slow_down`, `unavailable` or `internal`. Codes are added over time: show the message of a code you don't recognise.

message.description: A plain sentence for the person using the app, written by the server.
examples: The model didn't respond for 60 seconds.

detail.description: The technical cause, for a Details view.

MessageKind.description: Agent messages only. A `reply` is part of the answer. A `note` is the agent's commentary while it works, such as "I'll check current prices first."; an app may show notes as live detail instead of in the conversation. Hide a kind you don't recognise.

Message.description: One message in the conversation. Messages are ordered by when they began.

role.description: `user` for what you send, `agent` for what the agent writes.

turn.description: Agent messages only: the turn that wrote it.

text.description: GitHub-flavoured Markdown, exactly as written. While a message is still being written, the text so far. Empty for a secret answer, for a message that only carries attachments, and for a reply that stands in for a turn that failed or was cut off before writing. A reply may hold `ari:` blocks, described in [the blocks schema](blocks.schema.json).

at.description: When the message began: when the server accepted it, or the agent's first word.

answers.description: User messages only: the ask this message answered. Any message you send while an ask waits answers it, whether or not you meant it to.

secret.description: User messages only: a secret answer, such as a code. Its `text` is always empty: the agent received what you typed, and the conversation keeps nothing of it.

attachments.description: User messages only: the photos and files you attached, in order.

spoken.description: Only on a message you spoke on a call.

ended_at.description: Agent messages only: when it ended.

outcome.description: Agent messages only. Absent while the message is still being written.

ticks.description: Replies only: the items you ticked or unticked in its plans, each at its latest. Absent until you tick one. An item without a tick is as Ari wrote it.

Tick.description: An item in one of a reply's plans, ticked or not.

part.description: The plan's index among the reply's `ari:` blocks, from 0.

PlanTicked.title: plan.ticked
PlanTicked.description: You ticked or unticked an item in a reply's plan, on any device. The agent hears about it with your next message.

AttachmentKind.description: `image` for a JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP photo, which the agent sees; `audio` for a recording, such as a spoken message's; `file` for anything else, which lands in the agent's workspace. Treat a kind you don't recognise as a file.

Attachment.description: A photo or file you attached to a message. Its bytes never change: fetch them once with `GET /v0/attachments/{attachment}` and keep them.

media_type.description: The media type it was uploaded with, such as `image/jpeg`.

width.description: Images only: in pixels, when the server could read it.

height.description: Images only: in pixels, when the server could read it.

StepKind.description: What kind of thing the agent did. Show the title of a kind you don't recognise.

Step.description: One thing the agent did while working on a turn: thinking, a web search, a command, an edit, a tool, a plan, a wait. Its title is plain words written by the server, safe to show as it is. Its other fields carry the specifics exactly as the agent used them (commands, paths, queries, URLs, output); show what you choose. Fields beyond the common ones belong to particular kinds, and a step carries those its kind has.

turn.description: The turn the step belongs to.

title.description: Plain words, such as "Reading notes.md": present tense while the step runs, past tense once it has completed ("Read notes.md"). A step that didn't complete keeps its present-tense title.

ended_at.description: When the step ended. Absent while it runs.

outcome.description: How the step ended. Absent while it runs. `completed`: it ran, whatever its result; a command that exits non-zero, such as a search that finds nothing, is completed, with its `exit_code`. `failed`: it couldn't run, or a tool reported an error. `stopped` or `interrupted`: its turn was stopped, or cut off by a restart.

duration_ms.description: How long the step took, once it has ended.

heading.description: `thinking`: the heading the model gave its reasoning.

summary.description: `thinking`: the model's summary of its reasoning, as far as it has been written.

queries.description: `web_search`: every query, when there were several.

url.description: `web_search`: the page opened or searched within. `tool`: what the tool made, such as the issue a gap report opened or added to.

pattern.description: `web_search`: the words looked for on a page.

results.description: `web_search`: results, when the search returned them.

command.description: `command`: the command line, exactly as run.

actions.description: `command`: what the command did, as far as the engine could tell: read a file, search for a term, list a folder, or run something else.

exit_code.description: `command`: its exit code, once it has ended. Non-zero doesn't make the step failed.

output.description: `command`: the end of what it printed, at most the last 2 KB, once it has ended.

from.description: For a moved file, where it was.

capability.description: `tool`: the capability the tool belongs to, such as a server's name.

arguments.description: `tool`: the arguments it was called with, as JSON.

detail.description: What went wrong, in the tool's or command's own words, when the step failed.

action.description: `memory`: `used` for the pages Ari drew on in this turn (one step, growing as it reads), `updated` for a page it wrote, `journaled` for an addition to today's journal.

pages.description: `memory`: the pages, by address and title, never their content. Past conversations show as one entry with the address `conversation:past`.

change.description: `memory` with `updated`: the change to fetch from `GET /v0/memory/changes/{change}` when someone taps it.

explanation.description: `plan`: why the plan is what it is.

items.description: `plan`: its items, in order, each with its state.

wait_ms.description: `wait`: how long the agent chose to wait.

AskKind.description: `question` asks for information or a choice. `approval` asks before the agent does something consequential, and shows a `preview` of what would happen. Treat a kind you don't recognise as a question.

AskOption.description: A suggested answer. Tapping it sends its `label` as your message.

label.description: A short answer, in plain words.

description.description: A little more about the option, when the agent gave it.

acts.description: Approvals only: present on the one option that goes ahead with the action, such as "Book it".

AskOutcome.description: How an ask ended: `answered` by a message, or `cancelled` by you before you answered, or because the agent asked something else. Treat an outcome you don't recognise as ended.

Ask.description: Something the agent asked you. Asking ends the agent's turn, and the ask waits as long as it takes: through the app closing, the phone going offline and the server restarting. The next message you send answers it, whether you tap an option, type your own answer or write about something else. At most one ask waits at a time.

question.description: Plain words, written by the agent.

options.description: Suggested answers, in order. Empty when only a typed answer makes sense. An approval has options, and exactly one of them `acts`.

allows_text.description: Whether to offer a typed answer beside the options. Always true when there are no options.

preview.description: Approvals only: what would happen, in plain text, to show before you agree.

secret.description: Whether the answer is a secret, such as a code. Send it with `answers` set to this ask: the agent receives it, and it never enters the conversation's history.

ended_at.description: When it was answered or cancelled.

answer.description: Present when the outcome is `answered`: the message that answered it.

StatusKind.description: Coarse, for animating the agent's presence. Show the label of a kind you don't recognise.

StatusLabel.description: Plain words written by the server, safe to show as they are. While a step runs, its title.

StatusDetail.description: Optional plain-word specifics, such as a search query.

Status.description: What the agent is doing right now.

LiveTurn.description: The turn running when a snapshot was taken.

inputs.description: The messages the turn started with.

read.description: Messages sent while it was running that the agent has since taken in.

retry_of.description: Present when the turn is a new attempt at a failed one.

status.description: The current live status, if there is one yet.

Snapshot.title: snapshot
Snapshot.description: The first event when the server can't resume from your cursor: there was none, the server doesn't know it (it was restored from a backup, compacted it away, or is a different server), or you are too far behind. Replace your view of the conversation with it. Its id is the id of the latest event, so resuming after it continues from here; it has no id while the conversation is empty.

reason.description: Why there was no replay: `no_cursor`, `cursor_unknown` or `too_far_behind`.

messages.description: The latest messages, oldest first, including a message still being written (with its text so far and no outcome). Page further back with `GET /v0/messages`.

steps.description: Every step from the first of these messages on, including the running turn's steps, in position order.

asks.description: Every ask from the first of these messages on, in position order, including the one that waits for your answer (it has no outcome).

turn.description: The running turn, or null when the agent is idle.

next.description: Messages waiting as Next, in the order they will be answered.

calls.description: The calls that started within these messages, and one still on.

topics.description: The topics Ari marked on these messages, in position order.

MessageAccepted.title: message.accepted
MessageAccepted.description: A message you sent is on the server's disk. Every connected app receives it, the sender included.

MessageQueued.title: message.queued
MessageQueued.description: The message can't join the running turn, so it waits as Next. It starts the turn after this one, together with any other waiting messages.

turn.description: The running turn it waits behind.

MessageRead.title: message.read
MessageRead.description: The agent has taken the message into the running turn. It reads new input at its next step, between model calls, so a reply it was already writing may finish first.

TurnStarted.title: turn.started
TurnStarted.description: The agent starts working. Stop works from this moment.

inputs.description: The messages this turn answers, in the order they were sent.

retry_of.description: Present when this is a new attempt at a failed turn.

TurnStatus.title: turn.status
TurnStatus.description: What the agent is doing now. It replaces the previous status, and `turn.ended` clears it.

StepStarted.title: step.started
StepStarted.description: The agent starts a step. It carries the step as it begins, with its present-tense title.

StepUpdated.title: step.updated
StepUpdated.description: More is known about a running step, such as more of its summary or its plan's progress. It carries the step as it now stands; replace your copy.

StepEnded.title: step.ended
StepEnded.description: A step ends. It carries the step as it finished: its outcome, duration, past-tense title, and what is known at the end.

MessageStarted.title: message.started
MessageStarted.description: The agent begins a message: its text is empty and it has no outcome yet. `message.delta` events follow.

MessageDelta.title: message.delta
MessageDelta.description: Text appended to a message. Text is never revised: `offset` is always the message's length before this piece.

offset.description: Where this piece starts, in UTF-16 code units.

MessageEnded.title: message.ended
MessageEnded.description: A message is finished. Its final text is its first `length` UTF-16 code units: everything streamed, or less when you stopped it, cut where it was on your screen. Its `ended_at` is this event's `at`.

length.description: The final length of the text, in UTF-16 code units.

AskStarted.title: ask.started
AskStarted.description: The agent asks you something. The turn that asked ends next; the ask waits for your answer.

AskEnded.title: ask.ended
AskEnded.description: The ask is settled: a message answered it, or it was cancelled. It carries the ask as it ended. When a message answers it, `message.accepted` for that message comes first.

TurnEnded.title: turn.ended
TurnEnded.description: The turn is over and its status is cleared. Nothing more about this turn follows.

MemoryPageRef.description: A page in memory, named but not shown.

MemoryAddress.description: Where something lives in memory: `memory:portrait`, `memory:now`, `memory:helping-you`, a shelf page such as `memory:people/alex`, a journal day such as `memory:journal/2026-10-25`, or `conversation:past`.

ChangeId.description: An opaque id the server chooses for one change to memory.

Call.description: A call with Ari, shown in the conversation as a block that opens and closes the stretch it covered.

position.description: Where the call started in the conversation.

ended_at.description: When it ended. Absent while it's on.

duration_ms.description: How long it lasted, once it has ended.

audio_deleted.description: True once you've deleted the audio of its spoken messages.

end_reason.description: Why the server ended it, in a line to show, such as "The connection dropped." Absent when you ended it.

Topic.description: Where the subject changed: a quiet label Ari puts on the message that changed it. A label used again is the same subject, returned to.

label.description: One to four words, such as "Florence trip", safe to show as it is.

position.description: The position of the message that changed the subject. Draw the label above it.

TopicStarted.title: topic.started
TopicStarted.description: Ari marked where the subject changed, while answering the message that changed it.

Correction.description: A word the server corrected in a spoken message, from what it has learnt: `text` from `offset` for `length` characters is what it meant, and `heard` what the recogniser heard.

Spoken.description: How a message you spoke on a call came to be: the call, its audio while it's kept, and the words the server corrected.

audio.description: The recording of what you said. Absent once you've deleted the call's audio.

CallStarted.title: call.started
CallStarted.description: You started a call with Ari. While it's on, Ari speaks.

CallEnded.title: call.ended
CallEnded.description: The call ended, with how long it lasted.

CallAudioDeleted.title: call.audio_deleted
CallAudioDeleted.description: The audio of a call's spoken messages is deleted; their text stays.

VoiceState.description: Whether the server can hold a call: `ready` once it can both listen and speak, with memory's vocabulary loaded; `loading` while it starts; `failed` when it can't, until the server restarts.

VoiceReason.description: Why the voice isn't `ready`, in a plain line to show, such as "The GPU ran out of memory loading the voice."

VoiceStatus.title: voice.status
VoiceStatus.description: The server's voice changed. Offer Talk only while it's `ready`, and otherwise show the reason. It's sent on each change after the server starts; `GET /v0/voices` has the state at any time.
